chunks: From him, from al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Kurdawayh al-Hamadani, who said:
I asked Aba al-Hasan عليه السلام about making up the witr, and he said: Whatever is after zawal, then it is shaf‘, two rak‘ahs by two rak‘ahs.

The correct approach regarding these reports is one of two possibilities. One of them is that we interpret them as referring to one who wants to make up the witr while sitting; in that case, it is appropriate that he pray two rak‘ahs in place of each rak‘ah, by way of what is more virtuous, though if he were to pray one rak‘ah in place of each rak‘ah while sitting, there would be nothing against him.

What indicates that is: 6 — What al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn Bahr, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Aba ‘Abd Allah عليه السلام about a man who becomes lazy or weak and so performs the supererogatory prayer sitting. He said: He doubles it, making two rak‘ahs count for one rak‘ah.

key_terms.الزَّوَالِ: the time after the sun passes its midpoint
key_terms.شَفْعٌ: an even-numbered prayer performed in pairs
key_terms.قَضَاءِ الْوَتْرِ: making up the missed witr prayer

ai.seo_question: How should the witr prayer be made up after zawal, especially if performed sitting?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the legal manner of making up the witr prayer after zawal and explains that it may be performed as shaf‘, two rak‘ahs at a time. It also clarifies, through another hadith, that when a supererogatory prayer is performed sitting, two rak‘ahs may substitute for one by way of greater virtue.
